GraphService（Python）

New parameter format

Python SDK Now wrap the complex input parameters into parameter objects. The advantage of this is that the field names are clear and it is not easy to pass multiple string parameters backwards. See: Python 参数对象 for complete field descriptions.

from atom_sdk import (
    CopyGraphParams,
    CreateGraphParams,
    ExportGraphParams,
    ImportExtensionNodesByPathParams,
    LoadGraphParams,
)

Only methods with many parameters and easy to pass errors require parameter objects; simple methods still pass graph_name: str directly.

method Input parameter format

create_graph

CreateGraphParams(graph_name, description=None)

copy_graph

CopyGraphParams(graph_name, new_graph_name)

load_graph

LoadGraphParams(graph_name, file_path)

import_extension_nodes_by_path

ImportExtensionNodesByPathParams(extension_nodes)

export_graph

ExportGraphParams(graph_name, dl_models_info=None, custom_nodes=None)

edit_graph_name

EditGraphNameParams(graph_name, new_graph_name)

edit_graph_comment

EditGraphCommentParams(graph_name, comment)

delete_graph / open_graph / release_graph / run_graph / clear_graph / get_timestamp

Directly transfer graph_name

get_graph_dl_nodes_model_info / get_graph_custom_nodes

Directly transfer graph_name

get_graph_workcell_models_info

Directly transfer graph_name, optional graph_node_id=

get_graph_json_data

Directly transfer graph_name

list_graphs / get_all_custom_subgraphs_no_thumbnail / get_all_nodes_info

requires no parameters

Recommended calling order

create_graph / list_graphs
        |
    open_graph          <- SDK Automatic caching timestamp
        |
   Edit node             <- see NodeService
        |
    run_graph           <- SDK automatic carry timestamp
        |
  release_graph / delete_graph

Interface detailed explanation

create_graph(params)

Create a new picture.

Parameter Object:
CreateGraphParams

field type Description

graph_name

str

New picture name, globally unique on the server

description

str | None

Optional, picture notes

Return value: dict[str, Any], usually contains graph structure and timestamp.

from atom_sdk import CreateGraphParams

result = client.graph.create_graph(
    CreateGraphParams("my_graph", description="Main diagram of detection process")
)
print("Created successfully,status:", result["status"])

list_graphs()

Get a list of summary information of all main images on the server.

graphs = client.graph.list_graphs()
for graph in graphs:
    print(graph.get("graphName"), graph.get("updateTime"))

copy_graph(params)

Copy an existing image.

Parameter Object:
CopyGraphParams

field type Description

graph_name

str

Source image name

new_graph_name

str

The name of the new image after copying

 
from atom_sdk import CopyGraphParams

result = client.graph.copy_graph(
    CopyGraphParams("my_graph", "my_graph_backup")
)
print("Copied successfully:", result)

delete_graph(graph_name)

Delete an image and clear the local timestamp cache.

client.graph.delete_graph("my_graph")

Deletion is irreversible. Please confirm that this picture is no longer needed before calling it.

get_all_nodes_info()

Get all node definitions currently registered on the server.

nodes_info = client.graph.get_all_nodes_info()
for node_type, info in nodes_info.items():
    print(node_type, info.get("description", ""))

get_all_custom_subgraphs_no_thumbnail()

Get an overview of all custom sprite templates.

subgraphs = client.graph.get_all_custom_subgraphs_no_thumbnail()
for item in subgraphs:
    print(item.get("graphName"), item.get("isCustomSubgraph"))

get_graph_dl_nodes_model_info(graph_name)

Get the deep learning model information that needs to be packaged when exporting the graph.

models = client.graph.get_graph_dl_nodes_model_info("my_graph")
print(models)

get_graph_custom_nodes(graph_name)

Get the custom node information used in the graph.

custom_nodes = client.graph.get_graph_custom_nodes("my_graph")
print(custom_nodes)

get_graph_workcell_models_info(graph_name, *, graph_node_id=None)

Gets the graph or workcell model information associated with a graph node.

workcells = client.graph.get_graph_workcell_models_info("my_graph", graph_node_id="graph_node_id")
print(workcells)

get_graph_bindings(graph_name)

Gets all binding names currently set for the graph.

bindings = client.graph.get_graph_bindings("my_graph")
print("output binding:", bindings.get("outputs"))

Return values ​​are usually grouped by inputs, outputs, init_params, run_params.

load_graph(params)

Upload and import this map file (.atom format) to the Atom platform to get a usable map. Before importing SDK will first read the current graph list. If graph_name already exists, will throw ValueError, /Graph/LoadGraph will not be called, and the existing picture will not be overwritten. You need to use a new picture name or delete the existing picture and try again.

Parameter Object:
LoadGraphParams

field type Description

graph_name

str

The name of the graph used on the server after importing

file_path

str | pathlib.Path

Local map file path

 
from pathlib import Path
from atom_sdk import LoadGraphParams

result = client.graph.load_graph(
    LoadGraphParams("imported_graph", Path("/backup/my_graph.atom"))
)
print("Request status:", result["status"])
print("Import progress:", result.get("percent"))

If the imported .atom package contains extended node files, the load_graph return value will contain extensionNodes. Just pass this field when importing the extension node. Do not pass the entire load_graph return value to the server.

from atom_sdk import ImportExtensionNodesByPathParams

extension_nodes = result.get("extensionNodes") or {}
if extension_nodes:
    import_result = client.graph.import_extension_nodes_by_path(
        ImportExtensionNodesByPathParams(extension_nodes)
    )
    print(import_result)

import_extension_nodes_by_path(params)

Import the extension node file described by the extensionNodes field in the load_graph(…​) return value. This interface only receives extended node mapping, do not pass in the entire load_graph return value directly.

Parameter Object:
ImportExtensionNodesByPathParams

field type Description

extension_nodes

dict[str, Any]

load_graph(…​) extensionNodes in the return value contains the information required by the server to import the expansion node

Return value: dict[str, Any], usually contains the request status.

from atom_sdk import ImportExtensionNodesByPathParams

extension_nodes = result.get("extensionNodes") or {}
if extension_nodes:
    result = client.graph.import_extension_nodes_by_path(
        ImportExtensionNodesByPathParams(extension_nodes)
    )
    print("Extension node import status:", result.get("status"))

export_graph(params)

Export graphs and related models, and expand node information.

Parameter Object:
ExportGraphParams

field type Description

graph_name

str

The name of the graph to be exported

dl_models_info

dict[str, Any] | None

Optional, model information that needs to be packaged together

custom_nodes

dict[str, Any] | None

Optional, custom node information that needs to be packaged together

 
from atom_sdk import ExportGraphParams

result = client.graph.export_graph(ExportGraphParams("my_graph"))
print("Download address:", result.get("url"))

open_graph(graph_name)

Open the main image and cache timestamp returned by the server. When later editing nodes, connections, and parameters, SDK will automatically carry this version number.

result = client.graph.open_graph("my_graph")
print("Whether to open for the first time:", result.get("firstOpen"))

edit_graph_name(params)

Modify the picture name.

from atom_sdk import EditGraphNameParams

client.graph.edit_graph_name(EditGraphNameParams("my_graph", "my_graph_v2"))

release_graph(graph_name)

Release the main image and clear the local timestamp cache.

client.graph.release_graph("my_graph")

run_graph(graph_name, *, timeout_seconds=30)

Run the entire main image, automatically polling internally until the server returns the completion status or waits for a timeout.

result = client.graph.run_graph("my_graph", timeout_seconds=120)
print("Request status:", result["status"])
print("Is it done?:", result.get("finish"))
print("Time consuming:", result.get("total_time"))

timeout_seconds=None means waiting until the server returns completion or error.

clear_graph(graph_name)

Clear the intermediate data left in the graph from the last run.

client.graph.clear_graph("my_graph")

edit_graph_comment(params)

Modify the diagram notes.

from atom_sdk import EditGraphCommentParams

client.graph.edit_graph_comment(EditGraphCommentParams("my_graph", "New process notes"))

get_graph_json_data(graph_name)

Get the original JSON structure data of the graph.

graph_json = client.graph.get_graph_json_data("my_graph")
print(graph_json.get("graph_data"))

get_timestamp(graph_name)

Get the latest timestamp of the graph from the server and synchronize it to the SDK local cache.

result = client.graph.get_timestamp("my_graph")
print("current timestamp:", result.get("timestamp"))

Usually there is no need to call manually, only when you suspect that the local cache and the server are out of sync.

Complete example

from atom_sdk import AtomClient, CreateGraphParams
from atom_sdk.core.errors import AtomApiError

client = AtomClient(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:10026")
GRAPH_NAME = "demo_graph"

try:
    created = client.graph.create_graph(CreateGraphParams(GRAPH_NAME, description="Demonstration diagram"))
    print("Create graph request status:", created["status"])
    opened = client.graph.open_graph(GRAPH_NAME)
    print("Number of graph nodes:", len(opened.get("graph", {}).get("nodes", [])))

    nodes_info = client.graph.get_all_nodes_info()
    print("Number of available nodes:", len(nodes_info))

    run_result = client.graph.run_graph(GRAPH_NAME)
    print("Run request status:", run_result["status"])
    print("Run completed:", run_result.get("finish"))

except AtomApiError as exc:
    print("Server error:", exc)

finally:
    client.graph.release_graph(GRAPH_NAME)
